You are applying the fix wave from the final whole-branch review of a completed visual redesign. Four findings, all in css/components.css. This is the only fix pass — apply all four in one commit. Working directory: c:\Users\leont\Desktop\CleaningSystem-main Git branch: redesign/warm-premium (already checked out — commit here, do not switch branches) SCOPE: modify ONLY css/components.css. Do not touch any .js file, index.html, scripts/, or anything under frontend/. Do not change any user-facing text. Do not reorder or delete existing layers — make targeted edits only. BACKGROUND YOU NEED: css/components.css is ~1257 lines built as six appended layers (tokens/reset/layout, header/footer, buttons/hero, cards, portfolio/prices/about, contacts/focus/responsive/reduced-motion). Custom properties are defined in the :root block at the top; use existing tokens, do not invent new ones and do not redefine any. There are exactly four `!important` declarations, all inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) — do not add a fifth anywhere. --- FINDING 1 (Important) — `:focus-visible` silently destroys the shape of two elements. css/components.css:1182 currently reads: :focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: 2px; border-radius: var(--r-sm); } `:focus-visible` has specificity (0,1,0) and sits AFTER `.tab-btn { border-radius: var(--r-pill) }` (~line 563) and `.modal-close { border-radius: 50% }` (~line 845), which are also (0,1,0). Equal specificity, later source wins — so keyboard-focusing a services category tab morphs the pill into an 8px rectangle, and focusing the portfolio modal's close button turns the circle into a rounded square. FIX: delete the `border-radius: var(--r-sm);` line from the bare `:focus-visible` rule. Keep `outline` and `outline-offset`. The outline follows each element's own border-radius in current browsers, so nothing is lost. FINDING 2 (Important) — three interactive targets are below the 44px minimum the spec requires. The spec (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-28-cleaning-site-redesign-design.md §9) states: "Interactive targets at least 44px in their smallest dimension." These three declare less: a) `.btn-card { min-height: 38px; ... }` (~line 351) — the "Order" button on every service card b) `.tab-btn { min-height: 40px; ... }` (~line 558) — every services category filter c) `.modal-close { width: 38px; height: 38px; ... }` (~lines 837-838) — the portfolio modal close button FIX: a) change `.btn-card`'s min-height from 38px to 44px b) change `.tab-btn`'s min-height from 40px to 44px c) change `.modal-close`'s width and height from 38px to 44px Change nothing else in those three rules. Two more targets are borderline and should be made explicit rather than left to computed line-height: d) `header nav a` (~line 222) currently uses `padding: 9px 13px` on 14px/1.65 text, computing to roughly 41px. Change it to a definite 44px WITHOUT growing the header: replace `padding: 9px 13px;` with display: inline-flex; align-items: center; min-height: 44px; padding: 0 13px; Keep every other declaration in that rule as-is. Sanity check the arithmetic: `header nav` has `padding: var(--s3) 0` = 12px top + 12px bottom, so 44 + 24 = 68px, which exactly equals the `--header-h: 68px` min-height already on `.header-container`. The header must NOT get taller. Confirm --header-h is still 68px and that you did not change it. e) `.lang-select` (~line 258) uses `padding: 8px 10px` with `line-height: 1`, computing to roughly 32px. Add `min-height: 44px;` and change its padding to `0 10px`. Keep its other declarations. FINDING 3 (Minor) — dead selector. In the focus-visibility layer (~line 1186) there is a grouped rule: header :focus-visible, .contacts-info :focus-visible, .price-card.featured :focus-visible { outline-color: var(--accent-on-ink); } `.contacts-info` (rendered by js/pages/contacts.js) contains only an `

` and four `

` elements — no link, button, or input — so `.contacts-info :focus-visible` can never match. FIX: remove ONLY the `.contacts-info :focus-visible,` line from that selector group. Keep `header :focus-visible` and `.price-card.featured :focus-visible` — both are live and correct (the featured price card contains an ``). FINDING 4 (Minor) — focus ring on the first nav link is likely clipped. `header nav` (~line 203) has `padding: var(--s3) 0` — 12px vertical, ZERO horizontal — combined with `overflow-x: auto`. The first link's border box sits flush against the scroll container's padding box, while the focus ring draws 4px outside it (2px offset + 2px width). Outlines are ink overflow, not scrollable overflow, so the ring's left edge gets clipped. FIX: change `header nav`'s padding from `var(--s3) 0` to `var(--s3) var(--s1)`. That is 4px horizontal — exactly enough for the ring, and it does not change the vertical rhythm. --- DO NOT CHANGE THESE — they were reviewed and deliberately accepted: - The four `!important` declarations inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce). Do not add, remove, or relocate any. - `--ink-2` is defined and unused. Leave it. - `.page-container { flex: 1 }` is inert but harmless. Leave it. - `.portfolio-modal` must NOT gain a `display` declaration, `.before-img` must NOT gain `width`, `.slider-handle` must NOT gain `left` — js/pages/portfolio.js writes those three at runtime and CSS there would break the before/after comparison slider. (`.slider-handle::after` legitimately has `left: 50%` — that is a different box, leave it alone.) - The `.page-*` identifier classes and `.features-section` are intentionally unstyled. Do not add rules for them. VERIFY (run these and paste the real output into your report): bash scripts/verify-redesign.sh; echo "EXIT=$?" → all 10 checks PASS, exit 0 grep -c "!important" css/components.css → 4 grep -n "border-radius" css/components.css | head -40 → confirm the bare :focus-visible rule no longer has one sed -n '/^:focus-visible {/,/^}/p' css/components.css → outline + outline-offset only grep -n "min-height: 44px" css/components.css → at least 5 hits (btn-primary, btn-secondary, btn-card, tab-btn, header nav a, lang-select, form controls) grep -n "min-height: 38px\|min-height: 40px" css/components.css → zero hits sed -n '/^\.modal-close {/,/^}/p' css/components.css → width and height both 44px grep -c -- "--header-h: 68px" css/components.css → 1 (header height unchanged) grep -c "contacts-info :focus-visible" css/components.css → 0 sed -n '/^\.portfolio-modal {/,/^}/p' css/components.css → still NO display declaration sed -n '/^\.slider-handle {/,/^}/p' css/components.css → still NO left declaration grep -n "^\.before-img" css/components.css → still only border-right awk '{o+=gsub(/{/,"{"); c+=gsub(/}/,"}")} END{print o, c}' css/components.css → the two numbers must be EQUAL git status --short → only css/components.css ENVIRONMENT: no node, npm, npx, or headless browser (python 3.14 only; command is `python`, Git Bash on Windows). Do not attempt browser verification, do not install anything, do not claim a browser check passed. COMMIT: one commit. Use: git -c user.email=leontachyan@gmail.com -c user.name=leont commit -m "fix: correct focus-visible radius override and meet 44px target minimum" REPORT: write to .superpowers/sdd/2026-08-28-cleaning-site-redesign/final-fix-report.md — each finding, the exact edit made with file:line, and the full verification output. Return ONLY: STATUS, COMMITS, VERIFICATION (one line), CONCERNS (one line or "none").

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
